# R1 Gal 1:1–2:14 — Moo Galatians BECNT
**Range:** raw lines 1870–2528
**Lines actually read:** 1870–2528 (cache slice complete; file lines 1–660)
**Claim count:** 46

## Claims

### C-R1-001
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Moo structures Gal 1:1–10 as the letter opening: salutation (1:1–5) plus occasion/rebuke (1:6–10); Galatians (with Titus) uniquely lacks a Pauline thanksgiving, reflecting urgency over the Galatians’ Christian identity.
- **quote:** "Titus is the only other Pauline letter that lacks a thanksgiving"
- **locus:** L1872
- **passage:** Gal 1:1–10

### C-R1-002
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, paul-apostle, douglas-moo, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Moo reads the doubled denial of human origin for Paul’s apostleship (apo vs. dia; plural vs. singular anthrōpos) as source vs. agency—“fountain-head” vs. “channel”—not mere style, while allowing Ananias/Antioch as non-essential human involvement.
- **quote:** "the ultimate source of his apostleship was not human; nor did he receive it from, or through, any human being"
- **locus:** L1900
- **passage:** Gal 1:1

### C-R1-003
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, paul-apostle, douglas-moo, moo-galatians-becnt]

- **quote:** "he was chosen as an apostle “through” Jesus Christ as he was manifested to him on the road to Damascus"
- **locus:** L1904
- **passage:** Gal 1:1

## Coverage summary

**1:1–5 Prescript:** No thanksgiving; doxology instead; apo/dia source-vs-agency; dia with Father+Son instrumental; resurrection → new age; South Galatian addressees; grace/peace inclusio with 6:16; 1:4 keynote (cross, present evil age, new creation); Servant/Isa background; text-critical notes (hēmōn placement; hyper/peri; optative vs indicative doxology).

**1:6–10 Rebuke:** Double anathema; agitators = circumcision/law for full standing; thaumazō as passion; “so quickly” temporal (+ possible Exod 32); live *in* grace of Christ; gospel as grace-faith blessings not anti-Caesar lordship; heteros/allos near-equivalent; anathema = wrath; 1:10 parenthesis against people-pleasing (agitators’ hypocrisy charge); Nanos rejected; Christou preferred in text.

**1:11–2:14 frame:** Thesis 1:11–12 (non-human gospel via revelation); structure as negative travelogue vs pillars for apologetic independence (paradigm secondary); 2:15–21 transitional.

**1:13–17 Conversion/travels:** Conversion+call; broad Judaism; zeal for written+oral traditions; set apart before birth (Isa/Jer); Son revealed *in* Paul; Arabia as Nabatea, slightly preaching; Acts 9 Damascus stay interrupted.

**1:18–24 First visit / Syria-Cilicia:** Three years from conversion = Acts 9:26–30; historeō = acquaint; James as apostle; oath; Syria-Cilicia = Tarsus then Antioch pre–famine visit; unknown to Judean churches in that period; “the faith” objective; Isa 49 echoes.

**2:1–10 Second visit:** = Acts 11:27–30 private consultation (~AD 45–47), not Acts 15; 14 years from conversion; Titus not circumcised; Agabus/revelation; one private meeting; “in vain” = fissure fear; false brothers at Jerusalem; pillars add nothing; same gospel, different focus; remember the poor (continue prior aid).

**2:11–14 Antioch:** After 2:1–10, pre–Acts 15, post–first journey; Cephas condemned by God; men from James ≠ “those of circumcision”; moral-impurity table-fellowship issue; hypocrisy of Jews/Barnabas; public rebuke; Ioudaizein as compelling full Jewish status; truth of the gospel through-line with 2:5.

**Acts alignments (where Moo states them):** South Galatia = Acts 13–14 churches; Arabia interrupt Acts 9 Damascus stay; 1:18 = Acts 9:26–30; Syria-Cilicia // Acts 9:30; 11:25–26; Gal 2:1–10 = Acts 11:27–30 (not 15); Antioch ~ related to Acts 15:1; Agabus Acts 11:28; Peter Acts 12 leave; James consistent with Acts 15 inclusion of Gentiles as Gentiles.
